title: Operator ceremony playlist and slice checklist (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operator-focused checklist + "playlist" for running small-to-medium canaries and A/B experiments across product + infra teams. The goal is to give on-call, product stewards, and release operators a short sequence of rituals they can follow reliably when activating slices, observing signals, and doing fast rollbacks.

Audience:
- Release operators / steward oncall
- Product managers running feature experiments
- SRE and Serving Runtime oncall
- Solutions / SE for customer-facing canaries

Scope:
- Phased exposures (0.1% -> 1% -> 5%)
- Short-lived A/B experiments (24–72h typical) and micro-canaries for infra/model changes
- Latency/cost-aware experiments (budget guardrails included)
- NOT covering multiwave enterprise migrations (>1wk, complex migrations belong to migration runbook)

Quick-play checklist (operator playlist) — follow in order:
1) Preflight (T-24h or earlier)
   - Confirm experiment ID, hypothesis, primary metric, and guardrail metrics in ticket (ticket: PRODROLL-210).
   - Validate the rollout configuration in Redwood Console: model variant, route, slice filter, and ramp schedule. Take screenshot.
   - Assign steward (who will own 0–24h monitoring) and secondary (SRE pager).
   - Create a short Slack channel #exp-<id>-ops and invite stakeholders (PM, steward, SRE, SE).
   - Update deployment doc stub with quick links: Confluence signal catalog, GitHub PR, rollback steps.

2) Activation (T0)
   - Switch traffic to micro-slice (suggestion: 0.1% or synthetic test cohort).
   - Post activation message: short template below.
   - Confirm ingestion of telemetry within 2 minutes (latency, error-rate, p95, cost-per-req).
   - Run golden-check prompt set (for LLM features) against canary variant (10–20 canonical prompts). Compare outputs to baseline qualitatively (quick spot-check).

3) Early watch (T0+0–2h)
   - Observe: p50/p95 latency, 5xx/error spikes, token rate, cost delta, model confidence / hallucination rate (if tracked).
   - Verify observability pipelines: traces, logs, canary-specific dashboards.
   - If any guardrail exceeds threshold (see guardrail table), revert immediately.

4) Ramp steps (0.1 -> 1 -> 5 -> 10% typical)
   - Wait at least 30–60m between ramps for latency-heavy features, 15–30m for lightweight config changes.
   - At each step: re-run golden prompts, check SLOs, confirm cost delta within budget.
   - Capture a snapshot of metrics and attach to ticket.

5) Stabilization and analysis (after target exposure reached)
   - Run full evaluation harness (automated A/B metric calc) and compile quick deck: top 5 metrics, anomalies, sample outputs.
   - If regression found, trigger rollback and fill postmortem template.

Operator templates (short)
- Slack activation message (paste once):
  "Activating EXP-<id> (short description). T0 now. Steward: <name>. Watch: latency, errors, cost. Dash: <link>. Revert: <who/steps>."

- Rollback message:
  "Rolling back EXP-<id> due to <metric> breach. Rolling to previous route/variant. Follow-up docs: <ticket>."

Guardrail table (operator quick thresholds — tune per-product)
- Error-rate (5xx or token-level failures): >0.5% absolute increase over baseline -> rollback
- Latency p95: >250ms absolute increase or 2x relative -> hold/rerun synthetic tests
- Cost-per-request (tokens): >30% increase and not explained by increased quality -> escalate (SRE + PM)
- Behavioral drift: new toxic/unsafe outputs in 1% of sampled prompts -> rollback and escalate to research
- Model fallback rate (auto-failover): >1% -> investigate routing/compatibility

Signal checklist (what to watch — minimal set)
- User-facing signals: 5xx rate, retry rate, session dropoffs, NPS/CSAT changes (if available)
- Model signals: hallucination/semantic-error alerts, perplexity / confidence proxies, rerank score shifts
- Infra signals: GPU saturation, queue/backlog growth, container OOMs, autoscaling events
- Economic signals: tokens/sec, cost/hour, burst credits used
- Observability: missing traces, delayed logs, metric pipeline lag

Slice selection heuristics (how to pick a safe micro-slice)
- Prefer synthetic cohorts (internal traffic, non-production) for infra/model patches
- For UX experiments pick geographically small, low-volume cohorts or internal beta users
- Avoid fragile cohorts that rely on single downstream service (unless testing that service)
- Keep basket of 3–5 micro-slices pre-approved for rapid experiments (list managed in Confluence)

On-call handover and escalation (ceremony)
- Steward runs minute-zero checks for 30m, then hands off to SRE on-call with a 1-paragraph summary in Slack and updated ticket.
- If SRE is paged, follow SRE runbook. SRE should notify PM and product steward within 10m of paging.
- Post-incident postmortem owner assigned within 24h of rollback.

Experiment retirement / follow-up checklist
- If experiment meets success criteria: schedule rollout plan and cost projection; create Rollout/Release ticket to extend exposure with canary controls.
- If experiment inconclusive: extend run (document why), or reduce sample noise (re-slice), or close with learnings.
- If failed: capture traces, sample inputs/outputs, and run full regression harness; notify stakeholders and schedule postmortem.

Mini runbook snippets (copy-paste when needed)
- Immediate rollback (operator steps):
  1) In Redwood Console, flip traffic rule to previous variant (or disable experiment route).
  2) Confirm traffic reflow and verify baseline metrics returning within 10m.
  3) Post rollback message in #exp-<id>-ops.
  4) Attach logs and metric snapshots to ticket and tag SRE/PM.

- Quick partial mitigation (if full rollback costly):
  1) Reduce exposure to 0.1% or pause traffic for risky slice.
  2) Switch to cheaper model-quantization variant (if available) or route to fallback model in Redwood routing policies.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Can we add automated golden-prompt runs into the Console ramp step so operator doesn't have to manually run them? (Linked PR: #482)
- Proposal: make a "micro-slice" preset in Console with default guardrails (latency, errors, cost) so oncall can pick quickly.
- Need one consistent metric for "behavioral drift"—working with Research to define sampling+detector.

Appendix: sample checklist (copy into ticket)
- [ ] Experiment ID and hypothesis stated
- [ ] Steward assigned
- [ ] Slack channel created and pinned
- [ ] Redwood Console config validated (route/variant/slices)
- [ ] Golden prompts prepared and attached
- [ ] Preflight metrics snapshot taken
- [ ] Activation performed (time noted)
- [ ] Ramp timestamps recorded at each step
- [ ] Stabilization analysis attached
- [ ] Final decision recorded (rollout/extend/rollback)

Notes / context: quick mental model
- Think of this playlist as the minimum viable ritual to keep experiments small, observable, and reversible. Treat it as living — steal the good parts, ignore the rest.
- This doc intentionally mixes tactical operator steps (flip the switch) with product-level decisions (success criteria) because rapid canaries often need both.

References:
- Signal catalog: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Canary+Signal+Catalog
- Ticket: PRODROLL-210
- Rollouts PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/482

Last note: keep this short and sticky. If the operator cannot recite the first 6 bullets from memory, the playlist is too long.
